The commentators note that the four acts cover a life completely, so no gap is left where another agency might operate.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan. The figures honoured alongside God in the city were understood to have particular functions, bringing rain or granting children or protecting a journey, so the case for them rested on specific competences. The classical commentators read this ayah as testing that case against the four things that actually make up a life, and note that the list is chosen to leave nothing over.

keyTerms.note: A connective marking sequence with an interval, unlike the particle for immediate succession. Repeated three times, it spaces the four acts across a lifetime rather than listing them as simultaneous attributes.

The pronoun is doing the work: they are called your partners rather than His, which quietly grants that the arrangement is a human one. The Quran uses this possessive form whenever it presses the claim hardest.

A formula that removes God from whatever has just been said about Him, used across the Quran directly after a false attribution. It functions as a correction rather than as praise, closing the sentence by clearing it.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Partnership was a precise legal idea in Mecca. Men went into a caravan venture together with agreed shares, agreed duties and agreed liability, and disputes over who had contributed what were settled before witnesses. Calling something a partner therefore implied a stated function and a countable share. The ayah asks for exactly that accounting, in the terms the audience used for their own ventures.
studies.didYouKnow: The question asking whether any of your partners can do such a thing occurs three times in the Quran. The other two stand side by side in an earlier surah, one about beginning and repeating creation and one about guiding to the truth. Here the same challenge is put once and made to cover a whole life at a stroke.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Completeness is the argument. If the four acts named exhaust what happens to a person, then nothing is left for another agency to be responsible for, and the case is closed by inventory rather than by refutation. That also has a consequence for the reader, since it means there is no stage of a life at which someone else is in charge. The same hand is described as running the beginning, the middle and both ends.

crossReferences.why: Puts the same challenge twice in succession, about originating creation and about guiding to truth.
Says those called on besides Him possess nothing, cannot hear a prayer, and will reject the partnership.
Sets the same test at its smallest, whether they could create or recover a single fly.

studies.applyIt: Take the four things this ayah lists and check which of them you have ever seriously imagined arranging for yourself: being born, being fed, dying, and what comes after. Most people have opinions about the second and avoid the rest. Just noticing which parts of your own life you actually think about is worth a few minutes.

studies.title: Corruption On Land And Sea
studies.meaning: The opening verb means to come to the surface and become visible, so the damage is described as surfacing rather than starting. It is then attached to what human hands have earned, using the ordinary word for acquiring. What follows is a stated purpose, and it is not retribution: people are made to taste part of what they did so that they might come back. Commentators differ over the scope of the corruption, some reading it as moral disorder among people, others as visible ruin in the world, and many holding both.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan. The passage comes shortly after instructions on giving relatives, the destitute and the traveller their due, and after a contrast between wealth grown at other people's expense and wealth given away. The sequence connects what people do with money to what happens to the country around them. Mecca lived on routes across land that could not carry much pressure, and on shipping down the Red Sea coast.

keyTerms.note: From the back or the outer side of a thing. The verb means to become outwardly visible, which implies the condition existed before it could be seen and is only now showing.
The ordinary commercial word for gaining something by effort, used throughout the Quran of deeds. It treats actions as acquisitions a person accumulates rather than as events that merely happen.
A plain verb of physical return, the same word used of coming home. Naming it as the purpose puts the whole clause inside an invitation rather than inside a sentence of punishment.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Both arenas were economic facts. Pasture near a settlement could be grazed past recovery in a bad year, and clans quarrelled over wells and sometimes fouled them deliberately. Trees around Mecca were cut for fuel faster than the valley replaced them. On the water, the Red Sea route to Abyssinia carried grain and cloth, and a lost ship took a family's capital with it.
studies.didYouKnow: Land and sea are paired repeatedly in the Quran as a way of saying everywhere people can reach: God's knowledge is said to cover what is in both, guidance is given through the darkness of both, and human beings are described as carried on both. Here the same pairing is used to mark how far the damage extends.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Consequence is presented as instructive rather than as settlement. Only part of what was done is tasted, and the stated aim is return, which places even visible ruin inside an invitation rather than a verdict. Responsibility is assigned to human hands in the same sentence that keeps the outcome within God's arrangement, and the passage holds both without resolving the tension between them.

crossReferences.why: States the same connection between misfortune and what hands have earned, and adds that much is pardoned.
Gives the reverse case, blessings opened from sky and earth had the towns believed and been careful.
Describes the return this passage hopes for actually happening, and then not lasting past the relief.

studies.applyIt: Pick one ordinary habit of yours whose cost lands on someone you will never meet: what you throw away, what you buy without asking how it was made, water left running. Change it once this week, deliberately, and notice how small the change is. The ayah's word for return describes direction, and direction changes before distance does.

studies.title: Each Prepares His Own Place
studies.meaning: An instruction to set the face toward the upright religion is given a deadline: a day that will not be turned back. Then the day itself is described in one word, people splitting apart. The next ayah explains what the splitting follows. Disbelief falls on the one who held it, and those who acted well are described as smoothing out a resting place for themselves. The commentators note the image: nobody is assigned a place on that day, they arrive at one they have been laying.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan, repeating the instruction about setting the face that appeared earlier in the surah and attaching a time limit to it this time. The commentators read the repetition as deliberate. The first statement described the human being's original disposition; this one adds urgency, which is the shape the surah takes as it moves toward its close.

keyTerms.note: A noun from the verb to return something, naming the possibility of reversal. Denying it of the day makes it a thing already dispatched, which is a stronger claim than saying it is certain to come.

From a root for a crack running through something solid, used of glass and of stone. The related word appears once elsewhere of a headache that splits the skull, so the image is fracture rather than sorting.
The verb for levelling ground before lying on it, or for preparing a cradle. It occurs once in the Quran, and it turns good action into groundwork, something laid flat now and lain on later.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Making camp began with the ground. Stones were cleared, a hollow was smoothed, sand was banked, and only then was anything laid down; a badly prepared spot meant a night without sleep. Everyone had done it, usually at the end of a long day when the work felt like an imposition. The comparison in the ayah would have been physical rather than poetic to its first listeners.
studies.didYouKnow: Both distinctive verbs in these two ayat are near-unique. The one for splitting apart occurs twice in the Quran, and its other appearance describes a drink in the Garden that causes no splitting headache. The one for smoothing out a place occurs only here. The same passage uses a word for fracture and a word for bedding down.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Consequence is described as construction rather than as sentencing. Nobody in these two ayat is given anything; disbelief settles on its holder and good action becomes a place already prepared. That makes the day of separation a revealing rather than a deciding, and it accounts for the deadline in the ayah before, since groundwork has to be laid before it is needed. The urgency comes from the nature of the work, not from a threat.

crossReferences.why: Uses the same warning about a day that cannot be turned back, with no refuge on it.
States the same principle, that no burdened soul carries the burden of another.
Says whoever does good does it for his own soul, and evil against it.

studies.applyIt: Do one small thing today whose whole benefit lands later: a saved file named properly, a difficult message sent early, ten minutes of something you are slow at. Then notice that you will not feel anything at the time. The ayah describes good action as flattening ground you will lie on, and groundwork never feels like arrival.

studies.title: Rewarded Out Of His Bounty
studies.meaning: A purpose clause attaches to the splitting described just before, and it names only one side of it. The separation happens so that those who believed and acted well may be repaid, and the source of the payment is specified: out of His bounty rather than out of what was earned. The commentators note that the earning and the paying are deliberately mismatched. A short closing sentence states what He does not love, and it uses the word for covering over rather than the word for erring.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan, closing the short passage about the day that cannot be turned back. The community being addressed was small and materially worse off than its opponents, and the classical commentators note that the surah keeps attaching outcomes to the believers at points where their present circumstances suggested otherwise. Nothing here is promised as compensation for a specific injury; the frame stays general.

keyTerms.note: A verb from the vocabulary of settling accounts, used of paying what is due and of returning like for like. Placing it in a purpose clause makes the payment the reason the separation happens at all.

The word for what is left over above a requirement, so it names excess rather than entitlement. Saying the repayment comes from this rather than from the account itself breaks the equivalence the previous verb set up.
From a root meaning to conceal, used of a farmer covering seed with soil and of night covering the land. Denial is described as burying something rather than as failing to find it.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Payment for work in that world was negotiated in advance and settled precisely. A hired man knew his wage, a guide knew his fee, and a share in a venture was calculated to the fraction. Anything beyond the agreed figure was a separate thing entirely, given at the payer's discretion and remembered for years. The distinction this ayah relies on was part of every settlement day.
studies.didYouKnow: The Quran says that God does not love a particular kind of person around two dozen times, and the list is worth noticing: the arrogant, the treacherous, the wasteful, the corrupters, the aggressors. What is named is nearly always a quality or a course of conduct rather than an individual, so the sentence describes a disposition rather than a group already excluded.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Two ideas are held in one ayah that are usually separated. Deeds are called an account to be settled, which preserves the seriousness of what a person does, and the settlement is then drawn from a surplus rather than from that account, which removes any suggestion that the outcome is purchased. The reward stays connected to the effort and stops being proportional to it. That is where the room for mercy sits without dissolving responsibility.

crossReferences.why: Names the same arrangement, wages paid in full and an increase added from His grace.
Repeats the pairing, the best of what they did rewarded and more given from His bounty.
Says He pays their wages in full and increases them from His grace.

studies.applyIt: Think of the last time someone paid you more than was agreed, or thanked you far past what you had done. Try to remember how it landed. This ayah describes the settlement of a whole life in that register rather than in the register of a wage, and knowing the difference from the inside is what makes the sentence mean anything.

studies.title: Winds Bearing Good News
studies.meaning: One sign is given four purposes joined in a chain, and the last of them is the destination. Winds are sent ahead as bearers of good news; then a taste of mercy, then ships moving by His command, then the seeking of bounty, and finally that you might give thanks. The commentators note the structure: three practical outcomes are listed and a fourth, which is not practical at all, is placed at the end as what the other three were for.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan. Wind meant two industries at once to this audience. It carried the smell and the cool that ran ahead of rain, which decided a grazing season, and it drove the ships along the Red Sea that connected Arabian trade to the wider world. The classical commentators note that a single sign is made to cover both the desert economy and the maritime one.

keyTerms.note: An active participle from the verb used for announcing something welcome, related to the word for skin, since good news shows on the face. It occurs once in the Quran, and it makes the wind a messenger rather than a force.

keyTerms.gloss: so He may let you taste
keyTerms.note: A causative of tasting, so the mercy is offered as a sample rather than delivered whole. The same verb runs through this surah for both relief and hardship, which keeps them parallel in how they arrive.

From a root the lexicographers connect with an animal that yields much milk on little pasture, so thanks is a large return on a small input. Placing it last makes it the yield the whole chain was for.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: The wind arrived before the rain did and everyone knew the signs. A shift in direction, a drop in temperature, the particular smell of wet ground carried from far off: herders read these and moved animals on the strength of them, sometimes days before a cloud was visible. At sea, the same seasonal winds set the whole calendar of sailing. Nothing in that world announced good fortune earlier.
studies.didYouKnow: The word describing the winds as bearers of good news occurs once in the Quran, in this ayah. The Book mentions winds often, as carriers, as scatterers, as a punishment and as a barrenness, but only here are they given the vocabulary normally reserved for the announcement a messenger brings.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The chain of purposes puts thanks at the end of a sequence that begins with weather, which makes gratitude the intended output of a physical process rather than an optional response to it. Everything between is genuinely useful, and none of it is dismissed. But the ordering says that a life which extracts all three practical benefits and stops there has missed what the arrangement was for. The last clause is the only one not phrased as a benefit received.

crossReferences.why: Describes winds sent ahead of His mercy, carrying heavy clouds to a dead land.
Names the winds as good news before His mercy, with pure water sent down.
States the arrangement plainly, that giving thanks brings increase.

studies.applyIt: Pick one thing that reliably goes right for you and trace it back three steps: the food to the shop to the lorry to the field. Do it once, out loud or on paper. The ayah puts thanks at the end of a chain, and the chain is what makes it possible. Gratitude without the chain is a mood.

studies.title: Binding Upon Us To Help
studies.meaning: A pattern from earlier history is set out in four steps: messengers sent, clear proofs delivered, retribution taken from those who committed crimes, and then a statement about the other side of the same event. Helping the believers is described as something binding upon God, using the language of an obligation He has placed on Himself. The commentators are careful with that phrase, reading it as a self-imposed undertaking rather than a claim anyone holds over Him. Nothing here is promised on any particular timetable.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan, addressed to a community that was outnumbered and under pressure and had not yet seen anything resembling relief. The classical commentators read the ayah as offering history rather than a prediction: this is what has happened before, told to people who could not yet see it happening to them. The surah opened with a reversal nobody in Mecca controlled, and this returns to the same theme from a different direction.

keyTerms.note: The word for a due or a rightful claim, placed on God by God. The construction occurs twice in the Quran, both times about rescuing believers, and both times the obligation is stated as self-assumed.

From a root meaning to disapprove strongly and then to act on it, so the word carries a judgement before it carries a response. This exact form appears five times in the Quran, and God is the speaker in every one.
From a root for cutting or severing, giving the word for a crime as something that breaks a connection. It names the act rather than the belief, which keeps the retribution attached to conduct.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: An obligation freely taken on was the strongest thing in Arabian society. A pledge of protection given to a stranger bound a whole clan, and a man who broke one lost standing that could not be recovered in his lifetime. There were no courts to enforce such promises; their whole force came from being publicly stated. That is the register the closing clause of this ayah borrows.
studies.didYouKnow: The Quran says that something is binding upon God in exactly two places, and both are about believers being brought through. The other stands in an earlier surah and speaks of saving messengers and those with them. Beyond these, the Book states many divine commitments, but this particular wording of an obligation is spent twice.
studies.theologicalSignificance: An obligation that a party places on itself is different in kind from one imposed from outside, and the difference matters here. Nothing constrains God, so the help described is not owed in the way a debt is owed; it is undertaken, which makes it a statement about character rather than about limits. That gives a reader something more durable than a guarantee of outcomes, since undertakings hold across circumstances that a prediction would not survive.

crossReferences.why: Holds the only other statement that saving the believers is binding upon God.
Records the promise fulfilled, messengers and whoever He willed saved and the extravagant destroyed.
States that He supports His messengers and those who believe, in this life and at the reckoning.

studies.applyIt: Think of a promise you made to yourself that nobody else knows about, and check whether you have kept it. Not a resolution, a promise. The ayah describes help as an undertaking freely given, which is the strongest kind of commitment there is, and the only way to understand what that weighs is to have made one yourself.

studies.title: Drops From Within The Cloud
studies.meaning: Rain is described as a process with six named steps rather than as an event. Winds are sent, clouds are stirred up, the cloud is spread across the sky as He wills, it is broken into pieces, and drops are seen coming out from inside it. Only then does anything fall, and it falls on whom He wills. The commentators note that the ayah keeps the agency at every stage while describing something the audience could watch happening. Joy arrives at the end as the human response.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan, in the surah's closing run of evidence. The commentators note that this ayah and the one before it approach rain from two directions, one from the wind that precedes it and one from the cloud itself. Nobody in the Hijaz had any means of predicting rain beyond reading the sky, and a whole year could turn on whether a particular cloud broke over your valley or the next one.

keyTerms.note: The specific word for drops of rain as they fall, distinct from the general word for water. It occurs twice in the Quran, both times of rain seen emerging from the middle of a cloud.

The word for something torn into portions, used elsewhere of the sky falling in pieces as a demanded punishment. Here the same breaking apart is what lets the rain through, so the image is repurposed.

A form meaning to receive something as good news, from the same root as the word for the winds a few ayat earlier. The whole passage is built around announcement, and the rain arrives as the message delivered.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Watching a cloud was a serious occupation. Rain in that country falls in narrow bands, so a storm could soak one valley and leave the next dry for another year, and people tracked a cloud's drift for hours to guess where it would break. Whole seasons of grazing depended on the answer. The clause about it falling on whom He wills described something the audience had watched go the wrong way.
studies.didYouKnow: The particular word this ayah uses for raindrops occurs twice in the whole Quran, and both places describe the same thing from the same angle: drops seen coming out of the middle of a cloud. The other is in a Medinan surah that continues into hail and lightning, so the pair covers a storm between them.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Describing a process in detail, rather than asserting a cause, is the argument. Every step named is one a person can observe, and the agency is placed inside the steps rather than behind them, so nothing has to be inferred from a gap in the explanation. That protects the claim from the fate of arguments that live in what is not yet understood. The more closely the sequence is watched, the more of the ayah is confirmed.

crossReferences.why: Holds the other use of the same word for raindrops, and continues into hail and lightning.
Traces the same sequence from winds to heavy clouds driven toward a dead land.
Puts the question directly, asking who sent the water down from the clouds.

studies.applyIt: Next time there is a sky worth looking at, spend two minutes watching one cloud rather than the weather in general. Notice that it has an edge, that it is moving, that it is changing shape while you watch. The ayah lists six stages in something most people register as one word, and the detail only appears if you stop.

studies.title: The Traces Of His Mercy
studies.meaning: A mood is described before it is reversed. The word for the state people were in just before the rain covers the silence of someone who has run out of argument as well as out of hope. Then the instruction is not to watch the rain but to look at its traces, at what shows afterwards: the green that was not there a week ago. The argument for a resurrection is offered as something observed every year rather than as a doctrine to be accepted, and rain itself is named as mercy.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan. The lines sit in a run of signs in the surah's second half, following the description of winds gathering clouds and of people's visible relief when rain finally reaches them. In Mecca the raising of the dead was the point most often ridiculed by the objectors, and the surah answers it repeatedly from things they did not dispute rather than from claims they had already rejected.

keyTerms.note: From a root joining hopelessness to speechlessness. It describes someone whose expectation has collapsed and who has nothing left to say, which is more specific than sadness.
The word for footprints left in sand and for the remains of a camp. It points at evidence left behind by something that has passed, so the looking is directed after the event rather than at it.
The causative of living. The same verb governs both halves of the sentence, the ground and the dead, so the identical act is described twice rather than one being compared to the other.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Rain in that country arrived rarely and changed everything within days. A wadi that had been dry stone ran, grazing appeared where there had been gravel, and whole clans moved to follow it. When the rains failed, families sold animals and went to relatives. The despair named at the start of this passage was not a mood in general; it had a season attached and everyone had lived through one.
studies.didYouKnow: The clause about the earth being given life after its death occurs three separate times within this one surah, at ayat nineteen, twenty-four and here at fifty, in almost identical wording each time. The surah returns to the same sentence at intervals, attaching it first to resurrection, then to rain, then to both together.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The case for the raising of the dead is made from a repeated observation rather than from authority, which makes it checkable in the only way available to a listener. Naming rain as the traces of mercy has a further consequence: mercy is presented as something with visible effects in the world and not only as a disposition held toward people, and the invitation is to read the ground for them.

crossReferences.why: States the same movement earlier in the surah and draws the conclusion directly: thus will you be brought out.
Adds the detail of the ground stirring and swelling, then names the same power over the dead.
Runs the argument through a human life as well as through the reviving of dry ground.

studies.applyIt: After the next real rain where you live, wait two days and then go and look at one specific patch of ground you saw before it: a verge, a crack in a wall, a corner of a park. Look at what has changed rather than at the weather. The ayah asks for attention to the traces, which are always slower than the event.

studies.title: A Wind That Turns Yellow
studies.meaning: A test is imagined and its result is stated in advance. Send a wind that turns the crop yellow, and the same people who rejoiced at rain would go on denying afterwards. The commentators note what this establishes: the earlier gladness was a reaction to weather rather than a step toward anything. Then two images follow for why. The dead do not hear, and the deaf do not hear a call once they have turned their backs on the person making it.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan, near the end of the surah's long argument from signs. The commentators read these ayat as the conclusion of that argument rather than an interruption of it: after a chapter's worth of evidence, the passage turns to explain why evidence has not worked. The condition described in the second ayah is not deafness in general but deafness combined with walking away.

keyTerms.note: An intensive participle for taking on a yellow colour, used of a crop drying out before harvest. It occurs three times in the Quran, and every one describes vegetation going over from green to withered.

A verb meaning to continue in a state through the daytime, so it describes persistence rather than a single reaction. It makes the denial a settled condition that the new circumstance does not disturb.

An active participle from the word for a back, describing people already in motion away from something. It qualifies the deafness in the ayah, so what is described is a physical direction as much as a condition.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: A crop turning yellow before it should was a specific kind of disaster. Barley and dates depended on water arriving at the right week, and a hot dry wind at the wrong moment could take a field that had looked promising for a month. Farmers watched the colour daily. Yellow at the wrong time meant a year of buying grain instead of selling it, and everyone knew the sight.
studies.didYouKnow: The participle for turning yellow occurs three times in the Quran. One is here, one describes plants that wither after water reaches them, and one measures the whole life of this world by a crop that yellows and becomes debris. All three use the colour as the moment a green thing has finished, and none of them is about anything else.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The passage distinguishes between a reaction and a change. Gladness at rain is real and is not condemned, but it is shown to leave nothing behind once the weather turns, which means it was never evidence of anything. Then responsibility is quietly relocated. Nobody is said to be incapable of hearing; the deaf in the image are those who have turned and are walking, so the condition described is produced rather than suffered.

crossReferences.why: Carries almost the same sentence about the dead and the deaf, in another Meccan surah.
Traces water to plants to their yellowing to debris, ending with a reminder for the understanding.
Uses the same yellowing to measure the life of this world against what follows.

studies.applyIt: Think of something that lifted you last month and ask what remains of it now. A piece of good news, a compliment, a day that went right. If nothing remains, that is not a failure, it is information about which of your reactions are weather. The ayah is about the difference between being cheered and being moved.

studies.title: You Cannot Guide The Blind
studies.meaning: The limit set on the messenger is stated a third time and then reversed into a positive. He cannot bring the blind out of their straying, and the only people he can make hear are those who already believe in the signs. The commentators note the order of the last clause, which puts belief before the hearing rather than after it. What is being described is not a failure of the message but the condition under which listening happens at all.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan, after years in which the message had been delivered publicly and refused publicly. The classical commentators read the sequence of ayat here as consolation addressed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), who is being told that the outcome was never his to produce. The surah has just finished a chapter's worth of evidence, which makes the placement pointed rather than resigned.

keyTerms.note: An active participle governed by a negating particle, so the denial falls on the role rather than on an action. The messenger is not said to have failed to guide; he is said not to be a guide in this sense at all.

A noun from the verb for losing the way in open country, where there are no landmarks and no road to return to. Straying in Arabic is a condition of being lost rather than a moral term borrowed for one.

From a root for handing something over intact and for being safe, so the word joins surrender and soundness. It closes the ayah as the description of those who can hear, not as a label for a community.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: A guide was a paid professional in that world, and an essential one. Crossing open desert without someone who knew the wells and the stars was suicide, and a caravan hired its guide as carefully as it hired its escort. A guide could lead a willing party anywhere. What no guide could do was move someone who would not follow, and that limit was understood by everyone.
studies.didYouKnow: This ayah and the one before it are repeated in an earlier Meccan surah, where they also come as a pair, and the wording is virtually identical throughout. The two versions differ only by a connecting particle at the start and one letter later on. The Quran contains very few passages reproduced at this length and this closely.
studies.theologicalSignificance: A boundary is drawn around what persuasion can do, and it has two effects at once. It relieves the messenger of an outcome nobody could deliver, which is the consolation the passage is offering. And it removes a certain kind of pressure from the reader, since a message that cannot be forced into someone is also a message nobody can be blamed for failing to force. What remains on the human side is delivery, and only that.

crossReferences.why: Holds the nearly identical statement in an earlier surah, closing the same way.
States plainly that their guidance is not your responsibility, though God guides whom He wills.
Names the role exactly, a reminder rather than someone with control over them.

studies.applyIt: Think of one person you have been trying to change, gently or otherwise, for longer than a year. Stop making the case for a month and see what happens to the relationship. You are not giving up on them. The ayah says the hearing was never something you could produce, and it is a relief to stop carrying that.

studies.theme: Time and the Brevity of Life
studies.title: Weakness, Strength, Then Weakness
studies.meaning: A life is described in three stages using one word twice: created from weakness, then given strength after weakness, then weakness again after strength, with grey hair named alongside it. The commentators note that the sequence returns to where it started rather than ending somewhere new. Then the next ayah moves to the Hour, where the same people swear they stayed only an hour. The two ayat set a life measured in decades beside a life recalled as a moment.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan. Old age in that society carried authority: the elders decided disputes, remembered genealogies and held the settlement's memory. But it also carried real dependence, since there was no medicine for failing sight or joints and a man who could no longer travel lost his living. The classical commentators note that the ayah names the decline plainly, in a culture that honoured age without pretending about it.

keyTerms.note: The same noun appears three times in one ayah, marking the beginning, the reversal and the end. Repeating a single word rather than varying it is what makes the shape of the sentence a circle.
The word for hair turning white with age, and it occurs once in the Quran. Naming a visible detail beside an abstract noun gives the second weakness a face, which the first one does not have.
The same word names the Hour of judgement earlier in the ayah and the tiny span the guilty claim to have spent. Setting the two uses in one sentence puts a whole life inside a single word twice over.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Life expectancy in that world made the arc short and visible. Children died often, and a man who reached sixty had outlived most of the people he grew up with. Strength was the working capital of a herdsman or a caravan man, and its loss was not a stage of life but the end of a trade. Everyone had watched a strong man become dependent within a few seasons.
studies.didYouKnow: The word for grey hair occurs once in the whole Quran, in this ayah. The word for weakness occurs three times inside the same sentence, which is unusual in a Book that generally avoids repeating a term so closely. The one detail that could have been left out is the one given only here.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Placing the two ayat together does something neither does alone. The first insists that a life is long and has a real shape, felt in the body across decades. The second reports that from the far side it will be sworn to have lasted an hour. Both are presented as true, which means the length of a life is not a fixed quantity but depends on where it is measured from. The claim about deception concerns the estimate, not the experience.

crossReferences.why: Runs the same arc through dust, seed, infancy and maturity to an appointed age.
Reports the same estimate on the Day, as if they had tarried only one hour.
Repeats the claim that it will seem like an hour of a day, alongside an instruction to be patient.

studies.applyIt: Ask the oldest person you can easily reach what surprised them most about getting older. One question, and then listen without steering. This ayah names a stage most conversations avoid, and the strange thing is that people are usually willing to talk about it and are rarely asked.

studies.title: You Did Not Know
studies.meaning: An answer is given to the oath sworn in the ayah before, and it comes from an unexpected quarter: those given knowledge and faith rather than from God directly. They supply the correct figure, that the stay lasted until this day, and then name the day itself. The last clause is not a rebuke but a diagnosis. Then the following ayah closes the exchange by saying that excuses will not help and no opportunity to make amends is offered.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan, at the end of the surah's treatment of the Hour. The commentators note that knowledge and faith are named together here as a single qualification, which is how the surah has been treating them throughout: the chapter opened by describing people who knew a surface and were heedless of what lay past it. The scene answers that description from the other end.

keyTerms.note: Read by the commentators as God's decree or His record rather than as a scripture here, since the stay is measured in it. Time is described as something already written down and consulted.
The phrase occurs in one ayah of the Quran and twice within it, once as the endpoint of the stay and once as the present moment. Saying it twice is what turns a term into an announcement.
A passive from a verb meaning to seek someone's return to favour by putting things right. Denying it says that the period for repair has closed, which differs from saying an apology was refused.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Disputes over how long something had lasted were settled by witnesses. Nobody kept dates in writing, so the length of a debt, a tenancy or an absence was established by men who could say what season it began in and what had happened since. A confident claim could be overturned by someone with a better memory. The scene here follows that procedure exactly, with a claim made and a correction supplied.
studies.didYouKnow: The phrase for the day of raising appears in a single ayah of the Quran, and it appears twice inside that one ayah. The first use dates the end of the stay and the second identifies the present moment, so the same three words function as a measurement and then as an announcement within one sentence.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Knowledge is given a role at the end that it did not have at the beginning. The correction is spoken by people, not delivered from above, which makes the scene a matter of one estimate being set against a better one rather than a verdict handed down. And the closing line separates two things often confused: the excuse is not rejected as false, it simply arrives after the point at which anything could be done with it. Timing, not sincerity, is what fails.

crossReferences.why: Runs the same exchange, a question about years spent and a correction that they stayed little.
Says excuses will not profit the wrongdoers on that day, in nearly the same terms.
Names those who received knowledge as the ones who see that what was revealed is the truth.

studies.applyIt: Try to say honestly how long you have lived in your current home, or how long since a particular friendship started, before you check. Then check. Most people are out by years in one direction. The ayah is about an estimate made with total confidence and corrected by someone who kept count.

studies.title: Every Kind Of Parable
studies.meaning: A summary is made of what the Book has done and then set against what would happen anyway. Every sort of comparison has been put before people in this Quran, and the surah has just spent most of its length demonstrating it. Then a hypothetical is offered: bring them a sign and the response is already known, an accusation of fraud. The commentators note that the word used is the one for people who deal in what is void, which is exactly the charge being returned.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan, close to the end of a surah that has argued almost entirely from things the audience could see. The classical sources record repeated demands for a miracle from the Meccan leadership, and the surah answers them here in advance rather than after the fact. Nothing in the ayah says a sign will not come; it says what the reception would be if one did.

keyTerms.note: The verb for striking, used across the Quran for putting forward a comparison. Making an example is described as an impact rather than an illustration, which is a claim about what a parable is meant to do.

A phrase claiming coverage rather than quantity, so what is asserted is range and not number. It appears four times in the Quran, each time as a summary of what the Book has already put in front of people.

From the word for what is void, so the accusation is not that the messengers are mistaken but that they are producing nothing. The same word appeared in the previous surah, there naming those who would have doubted.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Accusations of fraud were a standard tool in Meccan disputes and everyone knew the vocabulary. A trader who sold short weight, a claimant with no witnesses, a poet passing off another's lines: all were named with words for emptiness and hollowness. The charge did not require an argument, only an assertion, which is exactly what makes it useful and what the ayah is pointing at.
studies.didYouKnow: The claim that every kind of parable has been set out in this Quran appears four times across the Book, in four different surahs. Three of them are followed immediately by an observation about how people responded, and the recurring note is not that the argument failed but that the audience preferred to dispute.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The ayah says something specific about the limits of evidence. A sign is a piece of information, and information can always be reinterpreted by someone who has decided in advance what it means. Naming the response before it happens does not predict the future so much as describe a disposition already in place. That is why the surah spent its length on ordinary things rather than on spectacle: what it offers cannot be dismissed as a trick.

crossReferences.why: Makes the same claim of coverage and adds that most people insist on denying the truth.
Repeats it and names the human being as the most argumentative of things.
Says that even angels descending and the dead speaking would not produce belief.

studies.applyIt: Notice the next time you decide what something means before you have finished hearing it. A message, a report, a person's explanation. Try holding the conclusion for ten more seconds than usual. The ayah describes an audience whose verdict was ready before the evidence arrived, and everyone does a smaller version of that daily.

studies.title: Do Not Let Them Unsettle You
studies.meaning: Two sentences close the surah, one about them and one to him. The first uses the word for a seal pressed into clay to close a letter, a metaphor of finality applied to hearts that will not know. The second names a subtler danger than persecution. The verb means to make someone light, to unsettle them into haste or into taking themselves less seriously than they should. What is being protected is steadiness rather than safety, and the anchor offered is that the promise is true.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan, at the very end of the surah. The ayat just before it state that a miracle brought to the objectors would be dismissed as trickery, which describes a situation where argument has reached its limit. The instruction is addressed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and concerns the wearing effect of sustained ridicule rather than of physical danger. The commentators report no specific occasion for it.

keyTerms.note: The verb for pressing a signet into clay or wax to close something. It carries the sense of a document shut and marked, so that any later opening would be visible as tampering.
Built from lightness of weight. It covers being provoked into haste and being made to feel small at once, so what is warned against is losing gravity rather than losing courage.
From a root meaning settled knowledge that has stopped moving. Those described are not hostile so much as unanchored, which is what makes their company destabilising to someone who is anchored.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Seals were ordinary equipment. A merchant closed a sack or a letter with clay pressed by a signet ring, and the mark meant the contents were shut and any interference would show. Mockery was equally ordinary and far more dangerous socially: in a world where standing was held by reputation, poets were commissioned to make a man look light, and a successful verse could follow a family for a generation.
studies.didYouKnow: This surah opens with a statement about a specific near-term event, that the Byzantines, newly defeated, would be victorious again within a few years. It is one of very few places in the Quran where a political outcome is named in advance. The surah that begins with something to wait for ends with an instruction to wait steadily.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The closing instruction addresses morale rather than argument, which is itself worth noticing. The danger named is being destabilised by people who lack certainty, so confidence is treated as something that can be drained through company rather than only refuted. Patience here is not the endurance of pain. It is holding a position during a stretch when nothing in the visible situation confirms it.

crossReferences.why: Names the same pressure, a chest constricted by what they say, and gives a practice in response.
Addresses the same effect from the other side: let their speech not grieve you, since honour belongs to God.
Sets the measure for the patience being asked for, that of the messengers of firm resolve before him.

studies.applyIt: Notice the next remark that makes you want to move faster, post something, or explain yourself to someone who is not listening. Do none of those things for one hour. The word in this ayah describes being made light rather than being made afraid, and the test of weight is whether you can stay still while the remark is still fresh.
